note: Static explainers for Macro Engine pillars, keyed by engine row id. Content: Hercules (COLLAB.md spec, 2026-10-08). Update `live` as conditions change.

fiscal.body: Deficits, debt sustainability, sovereign spreads. Funds stress leaks into the currency.
fiscal.live: September's federal budget balance prints 1pm CT (cons -$34.7B). France: Oct 20 revenue-section vote, Moody's Oct 23 (rejection motion failed 236-149). The EU summit's €100B+ war-driven fossil import bill is the euro's winter drag.
fiscal.title: Fiscal & sovereign risk

growth.body: Who is accelerating, who is stalling (GDP, jobs, PMIs). Always comparative. Stronger growth pulls in capital and raises hike expectations.
growth.live: NZ BNZ PMI 56.5 — strongest since 2021 ex-one spike, 15th straight expansion — vs soft NZ card spending (-0.4%, 2nd fall). US industrial production today (cons +0.4%); China Q3 GDP Monday (cons 4.4% y/y). Australia jobs -39.3K, unemp 4.7% (5-yr high) still the antipodean drag.
growth.title: Growth differentials

inflation.body: CPI/PCE vs the central bank's target. High inflation alone strengthens nothing — what matters is what the bank does about it.
inflation.live: US import prices 7:30am CT (cons +0.8% m/m) — the pipeline after PPI's +1.3%; eurozone final CPI 4am CT (confirm-or-revise the 3.8% flash beat). NZ food prices flat (0.0%). With the Fed in blackout from Saturday, today's prints are the last inputs.
inflation.title: Inflation

policy.body: Central banks moving in different directions. It is the gap between them that moves currencies: money flows toward higher rates.
policy.live: Warsh's last word before Saturday's blackout was no word — 'I don't prejudge meetings'; October stays ~30%, the meeting priced as a hold. December pricing split (~67% vs ~90%+) — flagged. 10Y ~5.04% in Asia, softest in ~a month. Hammack hardened; Macklem leaned hawkish into Oct 28; Bailey dovish-leaning on the 2027 path with November (~86%+) untouched.
policy.title: Policy divergence

positioning.body: Where speculators already stand (CFTC COT, Fridays). Crowded trades are fragile: if everyone is long dollars, nobody is left to buy. The contrarian lens — where would a surprise hurt most.
positioning.live: TFF hedge-fund cut (report date Oct 6): no currency crowded — USD 54th, EUR 44th, GBP 48th, JPY 67th, CHF 41st, CAD 31st, NZD 55th percentile, all neutral signals. The split is AUD: hedge funds net long (79th) vs real money short (17th). The extreme is WTI — crowded short (5th pctile), squeeze potential on a shock. Next COT today.
positioning.title: Positioning

risk.body: Risk-on vs risk-off. Fear bids USD, JPY, CHF (havens) and sells AUD, NZD, GBP (risk proxies).
risk.live: Relief bounce: Nasdaq 100 fell as much as 3.28% intraday Thursday, closed roughly flat; Asia woke up green (Kospi +3.3%, Nikkei +1.9%). CoreWeave +6% on Huang's backing (bonds ~15%); BTC bounced to ~$82k. The haven bid (gold ~$4,172, CHF) is holding, not extending.
risk.title: Risk sentiment

tot.body: Export prices vs import prices: oil, metals. The same price moves two currencies opposite ways — say which and why.
tot.live: Escalation vs release: CENTCOM confirmed an Iranian projectile sank a Hormuz container ship; Houthis hit Aden — against the IEA's accelerated ~100M-bbl release (20M+ diesel ASAP) and US shadow-fleet sanctions relief under consideration. Brent-WTI spread compressed to ~$8.31 as the freight premium leaked; Hormuz clearance ~68% of baseline.
tot.title: Terms of trade
